thread:
emma_support: FYI, AcmePay reported a sudden auth+latency spike from EU customers since ~08:30 UTC. Ticket INC-12345. They see 401s then retries that hit billing. Can we triage? :grimacing:
raj_eng-network: Can you paste the curl + headers from the client and any X-Region / X-Pop headers returned? Also need dig from their ISP if possible.
mike_sre_oncall: Oncall checking infra now, oncall pinging edge telemetry and recent deployments.
emma_support: Minimal repro from customer (Frankfurt home ISP):
  curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
Response headers:
  x-edge-pop: iad1
  x-region: us-east-1
  x-request-id: r12345
Response: 401 Unauthorized, then 429 after retries.
raj_eng-network: Whoa — x-edge-pop iad1 for EU user. That implies DNS answer landed on US pop. Do we have recent geoip/route changes?
geo-sync-bot: GeoIP database sync failed for EU shard at 2025-06-04T08:28:10Z, retry scheduled in 5m.
linda_cs: Customer says this started exactly at 08:30 UTC. They lost ~2000 successful requests then auth failures and billing noise. They're asking for mitigation now.
raj_eng-network: Asking network team: run dig with +short and edns-subnet from their public resolver. Example we want: dig @<their-resolver> api.redwood.example +short +edns=0xff00:1234
emma_support: I got a dig from their ISP (added edns-client-subnet):
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> @resolver.isp.net api.redwood.example +short +edns=0xff00:1.2.3.0/24
203.0.113.45
TTL 60
-> Answer is 203.0.113.45 (us-east edge)
raj_eng-network: Can someone traceroute from a Frankfurt test host? Need to see BGP path and whether anycast answered in us-east.
mike_sre_oncall: Traceroute from eu-prober-01 -> first hop into cloud provider, then transit to us-east; AS path shows a recent prepull to us-east due to fallback policy when eu shard failed. Looks like failure cascade: GeoIP shard lag -> resolver prefills -> resolver cache shields -> many EU clients hit US pop.
emma_support: Customer reports auth tokens are region-scoped and fail when they hit a different region (401). Explains auth + retry billing.
linda_cs: Customer is asking for a short-term fix: can we force them to eu-pop or revert to previous fallback behavior?
raj_eng-network: Immediate mitigations: 1) Roll back last geoip table push for EU shard (if available) 2) Push a routing override for acmepay tenant to prefer eu pool 3) Invalidate resolver-prefill cache entries at edge (TTL 60) -> flush. Which is fastest?
mike_sre_oncall: Rollback geoip sync first (takes ~2-3m to re-evaluate routing). I'll trigger rollback now and kick an edge cache flush for the affected hostnames.
geo-sync-bot: Rollback initiated by mike_sre_oncall at 2025-06-04T08:40:12Z.
mike_sre_oncall: Done. Edge flush command run: 
  rtx edge flush --host api.redwood.example --pop iad1 --reason "rollback geoip sync"
raj_eng-network: Also toggled short-term routing override for AcmePay: tenant.routing.acmepay.prefer_pops = [fra1, ams1] (deployed to control-plane). This will route new connections to EU pools even if resolver answered a US IP.
emma_support: Customer retried at 08:43 and reports 401s dropped to near zero, latency normalized. They saw some billing retries but are OK with our mitigation while we root-cause. :thumbsup:
linda_cs: I'll update the ticket and offer credit for billing spike. Please add notes on TTL / resolver prefilling so CS can explain.
raj_eng-network: Root cause hypothesis: GeoIP DB sync job returned partial/stale data for EU shard -> downstream resolver prefill used wrong answers -> long-lived resolver caches + ISP caches caused proportion of EU clients to land on US POP -> region-scoped auth tokens invalid -> retries caused billing spike.
mike_sre_oncall: Action items: 1) Add verification step for geoip sync to confirm all EU shards succeeded before cutover. 2) Reduce prefill TTL while a shard is in sync state. 3) Add alert on mismatch between source geolocation and allocated pop in edge telemetry.
emma_support: Noted. I'll add to INC-12345 and link to the rollout that triggered geoip change (RL-2025-0604-geo).
raj_eng-network: Anyone test edns-client-subnet strip effects? Some ISPs strip ECS and that can complicate routing; we should record which resolvers returned incorrect answers.
mike_sre_oncall: I'll attach traceroutes and edge spans to the postmortem. For now, incident closed — mitigation successful. :eyes:
emma_support: Closing thread for now, keeping postmortem and follow-up tasks assigned. Thanks all. :heart:
